texts.preamble: Chandan Mal & Anr. vs State Of Rajasthan & Anr. on 6 August, 2015 Author: Vijay Bishnoi Bench: Vijay Bishnoi 1 S.B. Criminal Misc. Petition No.2203/2015 Chandan Mal & Anr. V/S State of Rajasthan & Anr. Date of order : 06.08.2015 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vijay Bishnoi Mr S.D. Purohit, for petitioner.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that though against the impugned order dated 10.07.2015, there is a provision of appeal before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal as per the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, however, till date, the appellate tribunal has not been constituted and, therefore, he has challenged the impugned order by way of filing this criminal misc. petition wherein a prayer has also been made to issue directions to the respondent-State to constitute Food Safety Appellate Tribunal under the Act of 2006. On merits, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that though the Food Safety Officer in his inspection report has submitted that the sample of boiled milk with dry fruits and sugar, collected from the shop of petitioner, violates the provisions of Section 26(2)(II) of the Act of 2006, but no specific violation has been mentioned in the said report.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that though against the impugned order dated 10.07.2015, there is a provision of appeal before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal as per the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, however, till date, the appellate tribunal has not been constituted and, therefore, he has challenged the impugned order by way of filing this criminal misc. petition wherein a prayer has also been made to issue directions to the respondent-State to constitute Food Safety Appellate Tribunal under the Act of 2006. On merits, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that though the Food Safety Officer in his inspection report has submitted that the sample of boiled milk with dry fruits and sugar, collected from the shop of petitioner, violates the provisions of Section 26(2)(II) of the Act of 2006, but no specific violation has been mentioned in the said report.
